- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Deployed and live on Azure.

**URL:** https://umami-acsb2c83588.wittyplant-de1a228e.eastus2.azurecontainerapps.io — returns HTTP 200 (`<title>Umami</title>`), `/api/heartbeat` → `{"ok":true}`, `/script.js` → 200.

## What was created (all in `rg-umami-acsb2c83588`, eastus2)

| Resource | Name |
|---|---|
| Container App (external ingress, port 3000, 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, 1 replica) | `umami-acsb2c83588` |
| Container Apps environment | `cae-acsb2c83588` |
| PostgreSQL Flexible Server 16 (Standard_B1ms, 32 GB) | `pg-umami-acsb2c83588` |

Image is the digest pin from the folder's compose file, re-resolved before deploy and unchanged: `docker.umami.is/umami-software/umami@sha256:fa32d116…`. The repo's redu/AWS/GCP notes were used only for app-level facts (image, port 3000, `APP_SECRET`, no ClickHouse, no migrate command); the redu dname `umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud` was overridden as instructed.

**Credentials — store these, they are not written to any file in the repo:**
- Umami admin: `admin` / `[REDACTED:value]` — the documented default (`admin`/`umami`) was rotated as soon as the app went healthy and now returns 401.
- `APP_SECRET` (set explicitly, so sessions survive a DB password rotation): `[REDACTED:value]`
- Postgres `umamiadmin` password: `[REDACTED:value]`

Both secrets are stored as Container App secrets and injected as `DATABASE_URL` / `APP_SECRET`.

## Two things worth recording for the next Azure run
1. **Postgres Flexible Server is not offerable in `eastus`** on this subscription — the capabilities API returns empty edition/version lists there, so `Version` fails with `ParameterOutOfRange: should be in: []`. `eastus2` (and westus2/centralus/westeurope/northeurope/canadacentral/uksouth) work. Everything was placed in eastus2.
2. **Umami's `01_init` migration needs `pgcrypto`, which Azure blocks by default.** The first boot crash-looped with Prisma `P3009` after the migration died on `extension "pgcrypto" is not allow-listed`. Fix: set the server parameter `azure.extensions=PGCRYPTO` (dynamic, no restart), then drop/recreate the database — Prisma will not retry a failed migration on its own, so allow-listing alone is not enough. Do this *before* the app's first start to avoid the cleanup.

Network access to the DB is via the "allow Azure services" firewall rule only; the temporary rule I added for my own IP to diagnose the migration failure has been deleted.

The `az` CLI was not installed in this environment (so the Azure MCP tools returned 401), so I drove the ARM REST API directly with the cached MSAL refresh token. I did install `azure-cli` via pip mid-run, but ended up not needing it. Nothing outside the resource group above was inspected or modified.
